previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, COPD, chronic diastolic heart failure, and tobacco use was admitted for altered mental status and hypoxia. She had been increasingly somnolent for weeks and was found to have chronic hypercapnic respiratory acidosis and hypoxemia, consistent with decompensated obesity hypoventilation syndrome and untreated obstructive sleep apnea. She had not used her CPAP for months and continued to smoke, limiting treatment options. Imaging showed pulmonary vascular congestion but no acute infection or edema. She refused CPAP and BiPAP therapy during admission. Her condition remained stable but unchanged, and she was discharged home with services at her request, with no medication changes and strong recommendations to resume CPAP and pursue smoking cessation.
